text: Gold fell about 3% Thursday to near $3,867, its third straight drop, as the dollar hit a 19-month high on bets for a December Fed hike.
Silver dropped about 3% to near $50.06 after briefly trading below $50; SLV closed down 3.28% at $45.12, and the gold/silver ratio stayed near 77.2.
Gold miners fell more than gold: GDX lost 3.95% to $81.84 and GDXJ 4.68% to $99.62.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 bp to 5.10% in the first full session after Veterans Day, helped by higher oil and a weak 30-year auction; traders now see a December Fed hike as nearly certain.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned; the stock fell as much as 14% before closing down 4.3%. QQQ ended down 0.32%, TQQQ down 0.93% and SQQQ up 0.94%.
Brent jumped 3.3% to settle at $95.82 after Trump said the US doesn't need a deal with Iran; this matters for NRGU.
The VIX rose 6.9% to 18.70, ending a four-day decline.
Bitcoin slid to near $71,000 Thursday evening, its lowest since Aug. 20, as higher yields weighed on risk assets.
